claims.statement: For every finite ordinary tree T and every original leaf v with support s, alpha(T-{v,s})=alpha(T)-1. At p=alpha(T)-2, writing H=T-{v,s}, W=N_T(s)-{v}, R=H-W, and q_v(j)=i_j(H)-i_j(R), the contract summand is q_v(p)-q_v(p-1), the favorable condition is Delta_p(H)+Delta_(p-1)(R)<0, and S is exactly the difference of the two tagged witness-hit shells at sizes p and p-1. A leaf is residual exactly when alpha(R)<=alpha(T)-2; otherwise alpha(R)=alpha(T)-1, so the permitted selector spans two local top-rank regimes.
claims.scope: Exact ordinary-tree identities at the frozen rank p=alpha(T)-2; no sign claim, residual premise, or theorem about the aggregate is included.
claims.reason: The identities follow by partitioning independent sets on v/s and on W, with exact coefficient extraction. The unresolved theorem is the resulting selected tagged-shell cardinality comparison. T_100 at order 403 provides an eligible fresh larger replay of every local identity, but computation does not prove the universal sign.

limitations: No proof or eligible counterexample for the complete aggregate sign was found.
The T_m family scan checks only m=1..40,50,60,80,100 and is not an all-tree census.
No Lean build was assigned or run; the exact reduction remains informal at this stage.
